Influent flows in excess of the design flow can be routed to a 300,000 gallon overflow pond for storage until flows diminish, when the excess flow is routed back to the headworks for treatment.

Effluent from the equalization pond is controlled at flow control structure A by sliding stop gates, from which flow continues to flow to control structure B, which has two pressure control valves to prevent backflow conditions in the outfall.
Solids are aerobically digested and dewatered to approximately 12 percent solids by a belt filter press, then dehydrated to approximately 90 percent solids using a sludge dryer.

During the dry weather season (generally May through October) and other periods, as needed, tertiary treated effluent is distributed to a water recycling system at Discharge Point 002, which consists of a 55,000 gallon storage tank, accompanying appurtenances, and a pop-up sprinkler system located on the Mendocino High School athletic fields.

Disinfected tertiary recycled water is pumped to the high school storage tank in a “batch” fashion, and each tank of recycled water transferred to the storage tank must be used for field irrigation before the tank is refilled from the treatment plant.
